about: The incident's front-page record, kept by incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis. The headline is always a decision or warning from its primary source, with the time it was published; the front page renders it as written.
title: Storm Charles, Lisbon: Wednesday 11 November 2026

headline.text: Web Summit's Day 3 (Thursday) is running: "today is officially Web Summit's biggest-ever day", the organisers say; Wednesday was cancelled
headline.at: 12 Nov 2026, 09:23 UTC (first posted 09:00:19, deleted and posted again 09:23:34; read 09:46)
headline.label: fact

standfirst: Lisbon has no IPMA warning in force: its last, a yellow sea warning, ran to 03:00 Thursday (IPMA's open data, read 03:03), after the orange sea warning ended at 21:00. The red rain ended at 15:00, the orange wind at 15:56 (CAP sent 15:55, which also left no red on the mainland), the yellow rain at 18:00. At 14:00 the airport's wind gusted 74 km/h, the strongest of the storm there; by 19:00 it was west at 20 km/h with pressure rising. Civil protection counts 1,630 occurrences on the mainland since midnight, 781 of them floods (as the press reports its 19:00 briefing). Not an all-clear. The government's alert situation for mainland Portugal ran to 23:59 Wednesday, as declared: no extension was published in the Diário da República (read 23:35).
thursday: Thursday is running, in the organisers' own words: «Today is officially Web Summit's biggest-ever day of content and meetups!» (Web Summit on Bluesky, posted again 09:23 UTC after a first post at 09:00; read 09:46). Fact: the organisers' own public post. Still unannounced by the organisers: which of Wednesday's sessions moved, the PITCH semi-final, tickets (the press reported on Wednesday that some sessions move to Thursday).
